title: Fixed Horizontal Runner and Stone Millroom Cutaway
description: One newly authored complete static regional millroom cutaway. A real open-ended dry race lies between two full supporting masonry walls beneath the room. A whole horizontal radial paddle runner sits on a low bearing foot and shares one continuous vertical shaft with the complete broad upper and lower millstones above. The lower stone has a genuine shaft passage and sits on two whole exposed transverse floor joists; the upper stone has a real central feed eye. A full open tapering hopper and narrow throat stand on independent complete rear posts, tie and side seats. The retained room has a true rear window, two short side returns, a rear floor patch and a thick pitched rear roof section; the front walls, floor boards and front roof are deliberately omitted to reveal the continuous lower-runner to upper-stone relationship. Finite section faces are closed, not unfinished surface holes. This is neither the old vertically oriented twin-rim waterwheel on an external A-frame nor a standalone hand quern relocated indoors, and no old wheel, building or stone mesh is imported. Three opaque PBR roles, metres Z up, whole horizontal envelope centred, one architectural cutaway zero scenes. Dry unoccupied regional-inspired artwork, not an exact historic reconstruction or operational plan. No water, grain, grinding process, shaft rotation, bearing fit, transmission, hydraulics, energy output, food hygiene, access, loading, structure or engineering safety capability. Rigging animation and interaction not made or verified.
